summary: Dylan Esler works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Buddhist Studies from SOAS University of London and completed his PhD at KU Leuven, where he has also served as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, and served as professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He served as director of the Nitartha Institute and Kamalashila Institute.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.
Dániel Balogh specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Dörte Kamarid specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing her MA supervised by Helmut Tauscher.

E. D. Hirsch is a scholar in philosophy who studied at Cornell University from circa 1946 to 1950. He held academic posts at Wesleyan University (circa 1954–1956) and the University of Virginia (circa 1966–2012).

E. F. Schumacher was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn, Columbia University, New College, and the London School of Economics, and under Edward Conze. He held posts at Columbia University (circa 1930–1932) and the University of Oxford (circa 1942–1944).

E. Gene Smith was a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Utah and University of Washington under Turrell V. Wylie. He worked at the Library of Congress and served as director of the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (circa 1999–2010).

E. W. Adikaram was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he served as principal at Ananda Sastralaya.
Eberhard Fischer is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Basel. He served as director of Museum Rietberg from 1972 to 1998.

Eberhard Sandschneider is a sinologist who studied at Saarland University. He held professorships at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and Freie Universität Berlin, and served as director at the German Council on Foreign Relations from 2003 to 2016.

Eberhard Schrader was a linguistics and history scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, and Jena, and was a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1876–1908).

Edeltraud Harzer is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Charles University and the University of Washington, and under traditional teachers. She held posts at Stanford, Indiana University, and the University of Texas at Austin as professor emeritus.

Edgar Howard Sturtevant was a linguist specializing in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. After studying at Illinois College and Indiana University Bloomington, he held posts at Columbia University (circa 1907–1920) and Yale University (circa 1923–1943).

Edgar Polomé was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Université catholique de Louvain from circa 1941 to 1949. He served as professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin from circa 1961 to 1990.

Edith Wyschogrod was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She earned her B.A. from Hunter College and her Ph.D. from Columbia University, later serving as a professor of philosophy and religious thought at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.
Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculty at Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from circa 1987 to 2006.

Edmund Hardy was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Heidelberg University under Kuno Fischer and habilitated at the University of Freiburg, where he taught before serving as professor at the University of Fribourg (1894–1898).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indology scholar who graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886. He subsequently studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.
